title: Tenant Observability Mapping and Dataflow Contract for Private Deploys
author: Lena Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document defines the standard mapping of tenant-scoped observability data to transport paths, retention tiers, and privacy controls for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. It is a binding dataflow and telemetry contract between Redwood Field Engineering, Customer Ops, and tenant owners. The goal is consistent SLO-driven instrumentation, predictable ingestion load, and clear controls for customer-sensitive telemetry.

Scope:
- Applies to all Private deployment modes (VPC, dedicated on-prem appliance, and hybrid control plane).
- Covers metrics, traces, logs, model inference telemetry (token counts, latencies), KV-cache diagnostics, and user-configurable application events.
- Excludes application-level business PII; see the data classification policy for mapping those fields.

Owners and Roles:
1. Field Eng (owner): runtime-telemetry@redwood.internal — responsible for exporter bundles, default sampling policies, and instrumentation SDKs.
2. Customer Success / Onboarding: cs-onboard@redwood.internal — responsible for coordinating tenant-level telemetry settings and acceptance criteria.
3. Tenant Owner (customer): provides required IP/VM-level network routes and confirms data residency constraints.
4. Security & Legal: reviewers for any retention/forwarding changes that touch customer-sensitive classes.

High-level principles:
- Least-privilege: Only telemetry required for health, billing, and quality should leave customer-controlled networks unless explicitly approved.
- Tiered retention: Hot (14d), Warm (90d), Cold (365d) default tiers with configurable extensions under contract.
- SLO first: Instrumentation should be calibrated to preserve latency and availability SLOs (see SLOs section).
- Deterministic sampling: All adaptive sampling decisions must be deterministic per-tenant to support reproducible debugging.

Telemetry taxonomy (standardized fields):
- metric: {name, tenant_id, service, shard_id, bucket, value, timestamp}  -- tag schema required on all exported metrics.
- trace: {trace_id, span_id, tenant_id, service, op, start_ns, duration_ns, status_code, tags[]}.
- log: {id, timestamp, tenant_id, severity, source, message, structured_fields}.
- inference_event: {request_id, tenant_id, model_name, model_version, seq_len, input_tokens, output_tokens, request_latency_ms, cost_tokens}.

Transport and collection paths:
- On-prem default: local collection agent -> internal aggregator (kinesis-compatible) -> optional forwarder to Redwood control plane (only when customer enables).
- VPC managed: VPC-proxied telemetry collector (TLS to collector at 10.0.0.5:4317) -> regional telemetry ingress -> short-term hot store in region.
- Air-gapped: File-based export (rotating compressed batches) with signed manifests, transferred by customer to staging appliance for ingestion.

Default exporter configuration (example YAML for VPC collector):
---
exporters:
  otlp/http_default:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-us-west.redwood.internal:4317
    timeout: 5s
    compression: gzip
    headers:
      x-rw-tenant: ${TENANT_ID}
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms
    send_batch_size: 1024
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
---
(Operators must replace ${TENANT_ID} with the assigned tenant identifier.)

Sampling and retention policy (default):
| Data class | Default ingest rate | Sampling policy | Hot retention | Warm retention | Cold retention | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| System metrics (runtime & GPU) | All | no sampling | 14d | 90d | 365d | High cardinality metrics aggregated to 1m
| Inference latencies & errors | All | tail-based adaptive (deterministic) | 30d | 180d | 365d | Keep full traces for anomalies
| User logs (app) | up to 10k/s | 1:10 deterministic sample by tenant | 14d | 90d | 365d | Customer can opt-in to full logging
| KV cache diagnostics | up to 1000/s | 1:100 default, on-error full | 30d | 90d | 365d | Only include non-sensitive keys
| Billing tokens & counters | All | no sampling | 365d | 365d | 365d | Required for audit & billing

Note: For JSON-compatibility of this doc, the above table is represented as a monospace table; operator tooling reads a canonical CSV maintained in the repo.

Data classification controls and allowed forwarding:
- Classified levels: public, internal, restricted, pii. Only public/internal telemetry may be forwarded to Redwood control plane by default.
- For restricted or pii telemetry, the default is: no export. If customer approves, restricted telemetry may be exported under an encrypted, auditable channel with HSM-wrapped keys and 7x24 access logging.
- Export approval process: 1) Customer submits telemetry-forwarding request 2) Security approves & adds constraint 3) Field Eng provisions export with dedicated KMS key and signed manifest.

SLOs and alert thresholds (tenant-facing metrics):
- Inference 95th latency per tenant: SLO=200ms (hosted), 500ms (private default). Alert: 95th > 700ms for 5m.
- Error rate (inference failures): SLO=0.5% p95; Alert if > 2% sustained for 10m.
- Agent heartbeat: missing heartbeat for 3x interval triggers oncall escalation.
- Telemetry pipeline lag (ingest to hot store): SLO=60s; Alert if >300s for 1m.

Rollout & acceptance checklist (tenant onboarding):
1. Pre-install: exchange tenant_id, required subnets, collector endpoint, and KMS fingerprints.
2. Install collector agent with default exporter config and set TENANT_ID.
3. Smoke test: produce synthetic requests that exercise inference path and check telemetry appears in hot store.
4. Validate SLOs: run 1k synthetic requests at expected concurrency and confirm latency/error telemetry and billing counters.
5. Security review: confirm no restricted class fields are present in exported telemetry.
6. Sign-off: Customer CS and Field Eng sign acceptance.

Upgrade and rollback guidance for telemetry components:
- Upgrade path: Canary release of new collector binary to 1 tenant, validate metrics/trace conformity and sampling determinism for 24h, then stagger 10% increments across tenants with health checks.
- Rollback: If the canary emits malformed telemetry or breaks sampling determinism, run 'collector rollback --version <previous>' and re-run smoke tests. Preserve existing logs for 30d for forensic analysis.
- State migration: When changing metric names or tags, publish a mapping table and enable dual-writing for 48–72h to allow downstream consumers to adapt.

Troubleshooting playbook (high level):
- Symptoms: Missing traces but present metrics -> check OTLP exporter headers (x-rw-tenant), batching timeout, and collector memory pressure.
- Symptoms: Sudden spike in billing tokens -> verify client-side batching parameters, and confirm no runaway test traffic.
- Symptoms: Slow ingest lag -> check aggregator backpressure metrics, disk pressure on hot store, and network egress throttles.
- Escalation matrix: field-eng oncall -> runtime infra -> security (if classification violation) -> customer success for customer comms.

Testing and validation harnesses:
- Use the telemetry-validation tool (internal) to replay a 24h sample of production-like telemetry and assert schema, sampling ratio variance (within 2%), and end-to-end latency under SLO.
- Regression tests to run on each collector release: schema validator, determinism checker, high-cardinality metric guard, PII redaction smoke test.

Appendix A — Example JSON trace event (sanitized):
{
  "trace_id": "a3f2...1b9",
  "span_id": "f8e3...c2",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "service": "inference-rt",
  "op": "generate_completion",
  "start_ns": "1657690471000000000",
  "duration_ns": "2300000",
  "status_code": 0,
  "tags": ["model:rw-7b", "shard:3"]
}

Related artifacts and references:

- telemetry-validation-tool (internal binary)
- customer data classification policy (see related pages)

Contact and support:
- Field Eng runtime-telemetry@redwood.internal (primary)
- Oncall: runtime-field@redwood.internal (pager duty)

Change control and exceptions:
- Any exception to default retention or forwarding must be recorded in the telemetry exceptions register with approvals from Security and the customer account team. Requests are logged and retained for 7 years.

This document is meant to be a canonical operational contract. Operators should reference the canonical CSV and the exporter repo for machine-readable configuration. For legal questions about forwarding customer-sensitive telemetry, engage Security & Legal before implementation.
